# Demo Project Intake

**Purpose:** Record the decisions needed to make one demo reproducible, safe, and easy to present. Copy this file to the project root as `PROJECT_INTAKE.md`; do not edit the blueprint copy.

**Instructions:** Start with `docs/demo-app-blueprint/PROJECT_SETUP.md`; inspect the request, conversation, brief, repository, and existing decisions before asking questions. Use `docs/demo-app-blueprint/supporting-docs/requirements-discovery-and-readiness.md` to interview the demo owner one focused topic at a time. Complete this project-root worksheet with the demo owner and technical owner. Mark every unanswered decision-critical field `TODO(decide)`, name its owner and whether it blocks the next phase, and never treat blanks as confirmation. Record recommendations separately from approved decisions.

## 1. Demo goal and audience

- Demo name: Laundry Shop Order Flow
- Audience and roles: `confirmed` — portfolio reviewers evaluating the single-shop customer–clerk–owner order flow; source: user response, 2026-11-08.
- Problem or capability demonstrated: `confirmed` — demonstrate the PRD's single-shop laundry order flow across Customer, Clerk, and Owner roles; source: user confirmation of PRD walkthrough and service model, 2026-11-08.
- Presentation date/window: `TODO(decide)`; owner: user/demo owner; does not block prototype planning.
- Success signal: `confirmed` — portfolio reviewer can follow the PRD five-minute walkthrough and observe both pricing examples, one-discount rule, loyalty stamp/reward, status audit trail, and saved weighed price; source: owner-confirmed Gate A read-back, 2026-11-08.

## 2. Scope and deliverables

- Deliverable shape: `confirmed` — mobile app prototype. Flutter was selected for the frontend on 2026-11-11; the 27-page browser prototype remains the visual reference. Source: user response, 2026-11-08, and Flutter frontend direction, 2026-11-11.
- In-scope walkthrough outcomes: `confirmed` — PRD's five-minute script; include Must + Should items in prototype; time simulation is optional; source: Gate A read-back, 2026-11-08.
- Explicitly out of scope: `confirmed` — online/in-app payment, WhatsApp/SMS, pickup-and-delivery, multi-branch operation, inventory, staff management, stacking discounts, printed receipts, and loyalty rewards on per-item services. Receipts are in-app only; no printer or receipt paper is in scope. PRD Must + Should items are in prototype scope; Could items remain excluded pending a later decision. Source: Gate A read-back confirmation, 2026-11-08; in-app receipt decision, 2026-11-11. The user later requested shared Clerk/Owner dashboards, owner order oversight and an audit trace, and an owner-managed category-specific service catalog. These extend the review prototype only; they do not authorize production behavior, and dashboard figures are deterministic fixtures documented as synthetic in this intake.
- Known limitations or simulated behavior: `confirmed` — synthetic data and local-only prototype state/reset; no real payment or notification external effects. Source: Gate A read-back confirmation, 2026-11-08. The UI uses natural product copy; the synthetic/local boundary is documented here rather than shown as in-app disclaimers.
- UI design direction: `confirmed` — adapt the supplied CleanPro-inspired mobile design spec at `docs/Requirements and designs/UI Design/design.md`, with separate role navigation and product-task hierarchy. Generic laundry-shop labeling. Existing Stitch export contains 13 standalone HTML mockups; unsupported scale/printer/SMS/sync claims are explicitly excluded. Source: Gate B read-back, 2026-11-08.
- External design reference/MCP policy: use only supplied local PRD/design/mockups; no external DesignMD/MCP use. Owner-approved local design direction; no third-party reference used.
- User-facing copy approach: `confirmed` — natural product wording written as a real shop app; no visible demo, sample, preview or local-only disclaimers. No total before weighing. The synthetic-data and tab-local state boundaries are documented in this intake, `AGENTS.md` and `prototype/README.md`, not shown as in-app banners; no unsupported external-effect claim.
- Default project sequence: Prototype -> Frontend -> Backend; backend optional. Prototype and the fixture-backed Flutter UI preview are confirmed; the full walkthrough, backend and hardware remain pending decisions.
- Phase owners and exit criteria: user/requestor is making scope decisions (formal title not supplied); prototype owner/technical owner and later phase owners `TODO(decide)`.
- Prototype record: Gate A/B read-backs confirmed by user on 2026-11-08. After rejecting the first prototype as visually mismatched, the user initially requested page-by-page delivery, then asked to generate all pages together for review. The old monolithic `prototype/` implementation was removed. The user then requested a full visual redesign against the supplied CleanPro-style references, choosing local licensed laundry photography and a calibration pass on Home, Login, Order Detail and New Order before the rest of the set. The user then asked for an app-like entry rather than a review index: `prototype/pages/index.html` is now Welcome, it leads to sign-in with email/password plus four role accounts, and every other view is reached through the app’s own links. There is no screen-index page. All 16 PRD screens plus Welcome, customer destinations, Clerk/Owner Home dashboards, owner catalog and oversight/activity pages, and an Owner More hub are reachable through navigation. Generated pages are static, local-only mockups. Phase 4 added the dashboards, read-only Owner Orders, Activity log and owner-managed category catalog. Later the user asked that catalog add forms be moved off the list pages; dedicated `add-category.html` and `add-service.html` routes now keep the category and service lists focused on their records and add actions. The current set has 27 pages and uses natural product copy throughout, with no visible demo/sample framing. Current browser evidence and limitations are recorded below. On 2026-11-11 the user requested a Flutter frontend; a fixture-based UI preview is implemented in `mobile/` and documented below. Gate D was confirmed for the UI-preview scope on 2026-11-11; owner review of both the browser prototype and the Flutter preview is pending.
- Repository and runtime: no Git root was found. The visual reference is a 27-page static multi-file HTML/CSS/JavaScript prototype, opened directly in a browser. A separate Flutter UI preview lives in `mobile/` for Android and iOS, with a browser target used only for local visual review; it is not a production app. No app backend, real authentication, persistent orders or hosted app is present. The browser prototype's catalog/audit state is tab-local `sessionStorage`; Flutter catalog edits are held in app memory.

## 3. Environment and data

- Setup and launch method: open `prototype/pages/index.html` directly for the static reference. Run the Flutter UI with `cd mobile && flutter run -d <device-id>`; for local browser review use `flutter run -d web-server --web-hostname 127.0.0.1 --web-port 8085`. Setup details are in `mobile/README.md`.
- Demo environment and owner: `TODO(decide)`; no shared or production environment approved.
- Data source: synthetic deterministic fixtures in the static prototype; the Flutter preview uses `mobile/lib/data/fixtures.dart` for catalog and dashboard content and `mobile/lib/data/seed.dart` for accounts, orders, vouchers, notifications and starting activity. No real customer or shop data.
- Seed method: bundled fixture lists, including the default four catalog categories and twelve services; no database seed.
- Reset method and safety check: Shop tools in the browser prototype restores the catalog and clears recent audit events; the Flutter preview resets orders, sessions and catalog when the app restarts. Neither touches shared or production state.
- Demo accounts and roles: PRD specifies four seeded accounts (Customer A, Customer B, Clerk, Owner). The UI exposes four account choices; the browser prototype treats them as navigation only, while the Flutter preview validates the fixed seeded credentials in memory. No real accounts are created.
- Secrets/configuration owner: `TODO(decide)` if a backend or external service is later approved.

## 4. Quality and safety

- Build, lint, static checks, and focused tests: the Flutter frontend uses `dart format`, `flutter analyze` and `flutter test`; the static prototype uses `node --test tests/*.test.cjs` and `node --check` for local scripts. Current results are recorded below. Physical iOS/Android device builds are pending.
- Complete walkthrough smoke test: PRD §12 provides the proposed five-minute path; implementation and test evidence pending.
- Authentication and authorization behavior: role areas are reached through Sign in → account chooser. The browser prototype is navigation only; the Flutter preview checks the fixed seeded credentials and routes by role. Neither is real authentication or authorization, and production authentication and row-level security remain pending.
- Sensitive data or external side effects: no real data or external effects approved. The static prototype and Flutter UI are local-only and use synthetic fixtures; Flutter references only bundled assets at runtime.
- What is mocked, disabled, delayed, or incomplete: orders, queue, vouchers, dashboards and activity history are fixtures; catalog edits live in app memory; order actions update screen state only. No durable order creation, backend sync, payment, upload, printing, scanning or notification delivery is implemented. Receipts are in-app fixture views only.
- Human approval needed before showing or sharing: owner review of the static prototype and the Flutter UI preview. Gate D is confirmed for the fixture-backed UI-preview scope only; later hosting/sharing, backend and hardware decisions remain pending.

### Gate A scope read-back (confirmed by user, 2026-11-08)

- Audience/outcome: portfolio reviewers evaluating one laundry shop's customer–clerk–owner order flow.
- Service model/roles: single-shop wash-and-fold; Customer orders ahead, Clerk weighs and processes orders, Owner manages shop settings. No pickup/delivery or multi-branch operations.
- Primary walkthrough: use the PRD's five-minute script—Customer A places an Express order with WELCOME10; Clerk weighs 4.2 kg, confirms the 8.40 subtotal, 0.84 discount, and 7.56 total, records cash, and moves it through Processing and Ready; customer sees the ready notice; Clerk marks it picked up and a stamp is earned. Customer B places a Normal order; Clerk weighs 8 kg and uses the single loyalty reward for 2.50 off 8.00 (5.50 total); then show order audit history and that a later Express price edit does not change an already-weighed order. Time simulation is optional.
- Prototype feature breadth: include the PRD Must + Should screens/features; PRD Could items are not included unless explicitly added later.
- PRD exclusions proposed for confirmation: in-app/online payment, WhatsApp/SMS, pickup-and-delivery, multi-branch operation, inventory, staff management, stacking discounts, and loyalty rewards on per-item services. Payment is recorded manually; no real charge is proposed.
- Success signal proposed for confirmation: reviewer can complete and explain the cross-role walkthrough and observe both pricing examples, one-discount enforcement, loyalty ledger effect, audit trail, and saved-price behavior.
- Confirmed demo boundary: synthetic data, local-only prototype state/reset, and no real payment or notification external effects. Detailed disclosure wording/placement and exact reset behavior remain Gate B decisions.
- Open but not blocking Gate A: Flutter vs React Native; implementation runtime; presentation date; formal phase owners. No runnable app source is present in the inspected project root.
- Gate A next phase (historical): proceed to Gate B discovery after this scope read-back. Gate B is recorded separately below.

### Gate B experience read-back (confirmed by user, 2026-11-08)

- Device: smartphone portrait first, 360–430 px; tablet/desktop deferred.
- Prototype form: local browser-based phone prototype, independent of the deferred Flutter/React Native native stack decision; high-fidelity clickable UI, not production code.
- Screen inventory (14): Login; Customer Home, New order, Order detail, Order history, Loyalty card, Notifications; Clerk Order queue, Weigh and confirm, Staff order detail, New order for customer; Owner Services and prices, Vouchers and the originally named Demo tools screen (now Shop tools). This is the confirmed prototype baseline; Phase 4 additions (Clerk/Owner Home, category page, owner catalog/oversight/activity pages) extend it to 25 app screens + Welcome for review.
- Navigation: distinct shell per role, with PRD demo-only role switch to reach the seeded Customer A, Customer B, Clerk, and Owner personas.
- Visual direction: adapt supplied CleanPro-inspired local design system; use generic laundry-shop naming; no outside reference/MCP.
- Feature adjustments: manual weight entry/adjustment only; no scale integration, pass-verification claim, or printer feature. Customer phone optional; clerk searches synthetic local customer fixtures and can enter walk-in name and phone; omit bag-tag/care-note fields, SMS and sync claims.
- States/validation: customer unweighed/weighed, valid/invalid voucher, cancel before drop-off, empty order/notification, loyalty reward available/unavailable. Clerk missing/invalid weight, voucher minimum/usage rejection, paid/unpaid, unpaid pickup warning, legal status progression, walk-in no-notification result. Owner service price edit preserving saved order price; valid/expired/used voucher; local time advance and reset confirmation.
- Accessibility/evaluation: visible validation and success/error feedback; keyboard/screen-reader labels, contrast, and minimum 48px touch targets. Review at 360px and 430px widths.
- Simulation/disclosure: all state local and synthetic. Payment recording and notifications are simulated; no real payment, push, SMS, or other external effect. Disclose on information sheet, before payment confirmation, and in resulting order/notification state.
- Reset (historical Gate B scope): the Owner screen originally called Demo tools was intended to restore deterministic synthetic fixtures in the current browser. The implemented Shop tools screen restores only the catalog and recent audit events; it does not reset customer/order fixtures or affect shared/production state.
- Branding: generic laundry-shop labeling; no real shop brand is established in the PRD.
- Gate B confirmation: user confirmed the read-back on 2026-11-08. Native framework and later implementation remained explicitly deferred at that time.
- Post-read-back note (2026-11-11): Flutter was subsequently selected and a fixture-based UI preview was requested and built in `mobile/`; see “Flutter mobile frontend evidence” below. This later direction does not change the historical Gate A/B scope. Gate D was later confirmed for the UI-preview scope; see the Gate D read-back below.

### Gate D frontend read-back (confirmed by user, 2026-11-11)

- Audience and demo outcome: portfolio reviewers evaluating the single-shop Customer–Clerk–Owner order flow; the frontend makes the app’s information architecture, visual system and role-specific navigation inspectable.
- Confirmed primary walkthrough for this gate: the fixture-backed UI preview, not the full five-minute script. Welcome → Sign in → customer, clerk or owner area, with the 27-screen inventory reachable through the app’s own links and role navigation.
- Included routes and features: 27 screens in 28 routes at Gate D confirmation — Welcome, Sign in, 9 customer screens, 5 clerk screens and 11 owner screens, including parameterized category and add/edit service routes. Static fixture content, an in-memory owner catalog with audit entries and reset on restart, responsive role shells and the shared design system. A fixture-backed in-app receipt view was added later the same day at the user’s request (`DEC-019`), taking the preview to 28 screens in 29 routes.
- Optional/later: the full five-minute cross-role walkthrough (durable order creation, weighing, status progression, payment recording, pickup and loyalty), time simulation, QR/barcode scanning and offline sync. These are targets, not verified behavior under this gate.
- Out of scope / not applicable: printed receipts and printer hardware, backend/Supabase-PowerSync, real authentication or authorization, real customer data, external payment or messaging effects, production deployment and physical iOS/Android device builds. Receipts are in-app only. Gate C architecture remains not applicable to the fixture-backed work.
- Fixture/mock contract, disclosure and reset: orders, queue, vouchers, dashboards and activity history are deterministic fixtures; order actions update screen state only; collected-order receipts are fixture records; catalog edits live in app memory and reset on app restart; sign-in credentials are unchecked. Only bundled assets are referenced at runtime. These boundaries are documented in `PROJECT_INTAKE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `mobile/README.md`; the UI uses natural product copy without demo/sample banners.
- Responsive and accessibility expectations: phone portrait 360–430 px, with a 360 px automated route sweep and representative 390/430 px review; bundled Inter Tight for real text metrics; visible labels, focus feedback and 48 px-plus touch targets; fixed navigation and the order dock must not obscure reachable content. This is not a full accessibility audit.
- Acceptance checks: `dart format lib test` reports no changes; `flutter analyze` reports no issues; `flutter test` passes 6/6. Tests cover catalog add/edit/hide/restore, the anchored Welcome action, Welcome → Sign in → Customer/Owner navigation, a 360 px customer-home check, the itemized in-app receipt and discount, and a 29-route layout sweep. Representative screens were browser-reviewed at 360/390/430 px without horizontal overflow.
- Assumptions for owner correction: the Flutter UI preview is the Gate D artifact; the browser prototype remains the unchanged visual reference; owner visual acceptance is separate from this gate confirmation. The in-app receipt is an extension of the same preview scope, not a printing commitment.
- Blocking unknowns or conflicts for this phase: none for the UI-preview scope. The receipt question is resolved as in-app only; no printer choice is required. Backend/offline sync, demo environment/owner and presentation date remain unresolved later decisions.
- Proposed next phase: owner visual review of the completed browser prototype and Flutter UI preview. Backend or hardware work only after a separate phase decision.
- Recorded confirmation: user selected “Approve UI-preview scope” on 2026-11-11; scope version v3; affected decisions `DEC-018` and `DEC-019`.
- Post-confirmation extensions (2026-11-13 to 2026-11-15, `DEC-020`–`DEC-027`): the preview gained the flat visual redesign, the account/Settings reorganisation, voucher copy, Orders filters and pull-to-refresh, the compact date-range calendar, sign-in validation, the in-memory order lifecycle with checkout, cancellation and Clerk/Owner parity, a 16-order seed re-anchored to launch day, the owner order detail and weigh routes, and removal of Shop tools. The preview is now 30 screens in 35 routes. These extensions stay inside the Gate D UI-preview boundary: no backend, durable order, real authentication or production behaviour is added.

## Superseded prototype evidence

The prior monolithic prototype was explicitly rejected by the user as visually mismatched, then removed before this page-by-page rebuild. Its old interaction/test evidence no longer describes the current files and is not acceptance evidence for the rebuild. Current page evidence follows.

## Current page evidence and review status

- Artifacts: 27 pages in `prototype/pages/` — `index.html` (Welcome) plus 26 app screens. `index.html`, `customer-home.html` and `new-order.html` are hand-built; the other 24 screens are generated by `python prototype/tools/generate-review-pages.py`. Shared tokens/base styles, compact app bar and floating icon-plus-label navigation are in `assets/css/tokens.css` and `assets/css/base.css`; feature styles remain separate. Open `pages/index.html` directly in a browser; all local assets load without a server.
- Visual system: locally bundled Inter Tight, an icy-blue wash, frosted white surfaces, 24–28 px card radii, large order IDs, teal completed states, amber current states and a black primary action. The shared shell is one compact top app bar; device status chrome is not simulated. Bottom tabs are equal width with icon plus label, and below 380 px every tab stacks the icon above the label. Customer Home is greeting + active order first, then offer and loyalty, with a black New order dock pinned above the navigation on Home and Orders. The generated Clerk and Owner screens use a denser shared card/heading scale; the counter-order customer fields use an even two-column grid. All visible pages use in-product language without demo/sample/prototype/preview/local-only disclaimers; this copy choice does not change the implementation boundary documented here and in `prototype/README.md`.
- Phase 1–3 history: the shared shell, type/spacing scale, Welcome/Sign in/Customer Home calibration, Home-and-Orders order dock, Clerk/Owner density pass, three-tab Owner navigation (Services/Vouchers/More), shop maintenance screen (formerly Demo tools), consolidated notices, conditional `review-pages.js` loading and a local favicon were completed and reviewed as a static set. These remain the baseline; Phase 4 extends them.
- Phase 4 additions: Clerk Home (`clerk-home.html`) and Owner Home (`owner-home.html`) dashboards with order, sales, queue and service analytics; Owner Orders (`owner-orders.html`) is a read-only seven-order view with status filters, search and expandable detail; Activity log (`activity-log.html`) shows earlier history events plus recent catalog events with actor, time and old → new values; Owner More (`owner-more.html`) is the hub for Orders, Activity log, Settings and Shop tools. Daily Summary was retired and its material is covered by Owner Home. Owner navigation is Home / Services / Vouchers / More; Clerk navigation is Home / Queue / New order.
- Dashboard fixtures: Clerk Home shows four deterministic KPIs, including 184.50 sales today, a queue mix and operational notes. Owner Home shows 412.80 sales, 22 orders, a seven-day trend, service mix and follow-up alerts. The UI presents these as shop-facing figures; the values are synthetic fixtures from `assets/js/dashboard-data.js`, not live shop takings.
- Catalog: the customer New Order screen is category-first (four image-backed categories: Shirts, Pants, Dresses, Bedding; twelve services). Choosing a category opens `category-services.html?category=<id>`, which lists that category's services with price, unit, duration and description and an on-screen selection summary; no order is created. Owner categories are listed in `services-and-prices.html`, with a separate **Add category** action opening `add-category.html`. Selecting a category opens `owner-category-services.html?category=<id>`, which lists services with separate **Add service** and **Edit** actions. `add-service.html?category=<id>` contains the service form for name, description/benefit, price, unit (kg/item/load), duration, optional image and availability; editing reuses the same page with `&service=<id>`. Categories and services live in `sessionStorage` for the current browser tab; changes appear on New Order and the customer category page in that tab. Images are resized in the browser into JPEG data URLs and never uploaded. A service without an image uses its category image, then a styled icon tile; a category without an image uses a gradient hero. Missing or unknown category IDs show a dedicated “Category not found” state.
- Activity log and reset: catalog actions are recorded as audit events with entity, action, actor “Owner”, timestamp and field-level old → new values; the log combines them with earlier history events and offers All/Catalog/Orders filters. `shop-tools.html` shows catalog state, a reload link and a Restore button that returns the default catalog and clears recent audit events. No shared, production or customer/order fixture is touched.
- Local assets and provenance: Inter Tight is bundled at `prototype/assets/fonts/InterTight-Variable.woff2` under SIL OFL 1.1 with `OFL.txt`. Laundry photography is stored under `prototype/assets/images/`; sources, authors and the Pexels/Unsplash licenses are recorded in `prototype/README.md`. Photography is illustrative and does not represent stored customer garment photos. No remote resource is loaded at runtime.
- Customer Home retains one synthetic READY order card and 5/10 loyalty progress, and highlights the WELCOME10 offer. Header notification bell links to the static notification feed. These screens are not connected services.
- Browser verification: all 27 pages rendered at 360×844, 390×844 and 430×844 (81 checks) with no horizontal overflow and no broken loaded images. The category list → Add category form → new category services list → Add service form → saved service list flow was browser-exercised with image selection/clearing, service editing, hidden-service styling, the cross-category edit guard and Shop tools restore. The audit trace recorded the test category with old → new values, and the new forms kept their submit controls reachable above the fixed navigation.
- Automated checks: 51/51 Node tests pass after adding the two screens. All local scripts in `prototype/assets/js/` pass `node --check`. Tests cover route reachability, separate category/service list and form routes, catalog validation/CRUD/audit, image fallbacks, session storage and CSS regressions (`[hidden]` guard, dashboard mix tracks).
- Current limitations: no backend, real authentication, order creation or persistence, payment, notification delivery, upload, time simulation, setting persistence, voucher redemption, live analytics or complete end-to-end flow. Prototype sign-in and profile switching are navigation mockups; credentials are not checked and Customer B is the same static view. Catalog/audit state is per-tab `sessionStorage` and disappears when that tab's session ends. Owner order oversight is read-only and cannot change status, payment or pickup. Weigh and confirm still offers Cash/Transfer/QR/E-wallet while Staff order detail lists only Cash/Transfer; no QR artwork is shown. The 27-page set is a local visual review prototype; owner review and presentation sign-off are pending.
- No Git repository is present, so a Git diff cannot be provided. The copied blueprint files were not targeted by edits; before/after Git proof is unavailable.

## Flutter mobile frontend evidence

- Artifacts: `mobile/` is a Flutter 3.41.1 / Dart 3.11.0 project with Android, iOS and web targets; the web target is used only for local visual review. `mobile/lib/app/router.dart` covers 30 screens in 35 routes: Welcome, Sign in, 13 customer routes, 6 clerk routes and 14 owner routes, including parameterized category, service, receipt, checkout, order-placed and owner order/weigh routes. Settings is shared by all three roles, and the staff order detail and weigh screens are shared by Clerk and Owner. `prototype/` remains unchanged as the visual reference.
- Design system: bundled Inter Tight, a shared theme, top app bar, bottom navigation, order dock and UI primitives. Customer tabs are Home / Orders / Vouchers; Profile, Notifications and Loyalty sit under Settings. Clerk tabs are Home / Queue / New order; Owner tabs are Home / Services / Vouchers / More, and Owner More contains Orders, Activity log, Shop settings and Switch account with no Shop tools screen. The top-bar account chip shows the signed-in account and opens a flat menu with Settings and Log out; Owner Settings adds a Shop settings link. Customer Home and Orders show the floating New order dock above the navigation. Welcome uses a scrollable hero with the Get started action and its caption anchored above the bottom edge; the hero photograph carries no sample order. Sign in keeps the email/password and account picker without a back link; the picker only fills the seeded credentials, and submit validates them before routing.
- Visual pass (2026-11-12): all role areas were redesigned from the earlier glassy layers to a flat Swiss-utility treatment that keeps the Welcome identity — Inter Tight, cool off-white canvas and petrol teal. Cards are opaque white with hairline borders, headings are deep-ink editorial type, teal is reserved for status and actions, and shadows are limited to the deep hero, image overlays and receipt paper. Top bars are opaque canvas with a bottom hairline; the account picker, account menu, Settings hub, help sheet and dialogs are flat surfaces. Shared tokens and components live in `mobile/lib/app/theme.dart` and `mobile/lib/shared/ui.dart`; dashboard primitives are in `mobile/lib/features/dashboard/dashboard_widgets.dart`.
- In-app receipts: collected orders LDR-0039 and LDR-0031 show itemized lines, discount, total and payment method from their recorded payment. The customer order detail shows a receipt summary and opens `/customer/orders/:id/receipt`; the receipt is a paper-style in-app view with no print, download or share action. LDR-0042 has no receipt until pickup and shows the “Available after pickup” state if its receipt route is opened directly.
- State and data: the seed in `mobile/lib/data/seed.dart` holds 16 orders anchored to the current UTC+7 shop day (Customer A 10, Customer B 5, one walk-in; initial requests `LDR-0051`/`LDR-0052`; next order `LDR-0053`). Orders, activity, sessions and catalog edits live in memory and reset on restart. Customer New order → Category services → Checkout → Order placed creates a pending order; customer cancellation is Pending-only; Clerk and Owner share accept, decline, drop-off, weigh/payment, ready and pickup. Vouchers, notifications and loyalty come from the seed. Dashboard KPI, chart and service-mix figures remain synthetic shop-facing fixtures; dashboard recent orders and customer order views read the session orders.
- Responsive and visual checks: all 35 routes pass the 360 px layout sweep. The account/settings pass rechecked the account menu, Settings for all three roles, Help & support, Profile and the three-tab customer navigation at 360, 390 and 430 px. Earlier, Welcome, Sign in, Customer Home/Orders/Receipt, Clerk Home/Queue/Staff order detail, and Owner Home/Service catalog/More/Order oversight/Activity log were rechecked at 390 px, with representative Customer, Clerk and Owner screens checked at 430 px. The order lifecycle pass checked Customer Home, the cancelled order detail and Checkout at 360, 390 and 430 px and a Clerk order detail at 360 px; a 2026-11-16 spot check confirmed the Clerk order detail and Owner Orders at 430 px. No horizontal overflow appeared at 360–430 px. The narrow customer bar hides the wordmark to make room for the account and notification actions, filter chips stay compact, order rows wrap service names, and scrolling to the end of Home and Orders clears both the floating dock and the bottom navigation. This is visual review evidence, not a pixel-diff or a full accessibility audit.
- Account and settings interaction checks (2026-11-12): the top-bar account chip opened the flat menu for Customer, Clerk and Owner; Settings opened the role-appropriate hub; a preference switch toggled; Help & support opened and closed; Profile opened from Settings with a working Settings back link; and Log out showed a confirmation before returning to Sign in. The customer navigation showed Home / Orders / Vouchers with no Profile tab. These are local UI interactions only.

Tests cover catalog add/edit/hide/reset, the anchored Welcome action and removed sample order, Welcome → Sign in → Customer/Owner navigation, a 360 px customer-home check, sign-in without a back link plus empty-field, unknown-email and wrong-password validation, the account menu → Settings → Help → log out flow, account and help-sheet outside-tap dismissal, the Orders filter sheet with Today, presets, the compact month calendar with separate Start/End fields, active-field-only date changes, month navigation and Clear/Use dates, combined counts and clearing, the arrow-button status chip scroller, initial skeleton and pull-to-refresh completion, pull-to-refresh presence on the 15 primary role routes, the itemized in-app receipt, customer voucher copy feedback and clipboard content, a customer place-and-cancel flow, the Clerk accept → drop-off → weigh/pay → ready → pickup flow, Clerk decline with a required reason, Owner lifecycle parity, and a layout sweep of all 35 routes at 360 px using the bundled Inter Tight font.
